title: Casper and the Safehouse
premise: Noor Thornbury has spent three years guarding a paranoid defector, Casper Voss, in a safehouse whose location only Noor knows. When the house appears on a real estate site with interior photos — including shots of Casper's face at the window — Noor realizes someone inside their own security firm sold them out. As extraction teams close in and Casper's handlers demand he be moved to a facility where his testimony will be buried forever, Noor must choose between the duty that built their career and the truth Casper carries about the firm's own crimes. In the end, Noor burns their identity to deliver Casper's evidence to a journalist, keeping only each other as the safehouse burns behind them.
about_author: Rosalind Eastwick is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for private security firms before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse whose location she refuses to disclose.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. During a routine supply run, Noor finds the safehouse listed online with interior photos — Casper visible at the kitchen window. The emotional beat is cold dread: every protocol Noor trusted is already compromised. Noor hides the discovery from Casper while quietly testing which of their firm's channels leaked, realizing the breach came from inside.

chapters.title: What Casper Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper reveals why he defected: the firm laundered intelligence that got an entire village killed, and his testimony names Noor's mentor. The beat is intimacy sharpened by betrayal — Noor's loyalty to the firm cracks against growing love for Casper. A surveillance van appears on the ridge; the leak wasn't accidental, it was bait to flush them both.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The firm's own kill team arrives under cover of a 'rescue,' forcing Noor and Casper into a night flight through frozen backroads with Casper's encrypted drive. The climax: Noor turns their weapon on their mentor rather than surrender Casper, and they barely escape as the safehouse is torched to erase evidence. The beat is love fully chosen over duty.

chapters.title: New Address
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Weeks later, in a rented room far from anywhere, Noor watches the drive's contents reach a journalist and the firm begin to fracture publicly. Casper offers Noor an exit — new names, no history. The resolution lands on quiet hope: for the first time, Noor unpacks the go-bag instead of repacking it, choosing a life with no safehouse but no lies either.
